chapters.1.meaning: The first two captains demand that Elijah come down. The third asks for mercy and survives.
chapters.1.lds: How does the third captain’s request differ from the first two orders?
chapters.2.meaning: Elisha picks up Elijah’s cloak and takes up his work. His first acts show both help and judgment.
chapters.4.meaning: The women ask for help and act on Elisha’s words. The Shunammite refuses to leave him when her child dies.
chapters.8.summary: The Shunammite returns and asks for her land. Elisha meets Hazael in Damascus. The chapter also records Judah’s next kings.
chapters.8.meaning: The Shunammite’s return shows how famine can cost a family its home. The king orders her property restored.
chapters.8.lds: What help does the Shunammite need after returning from famine?
chapters.9.meaning: Jehu uses earlier warnings to explain his killings. The change of king destroys two royal households.
chapters.10.summary: Jehu kills Ahab’s descendants and Ahaziah’s relatives. He traps Baal’s worshipers and kills them. Yet he keeps Jeroboam’s golden calves.
chapters.10.meaning: Jehu ends Ahab’s royal line and Baal’s temple worship. His own worship still draws criticism.
chapters.13.meaning: Jehoahaz asks God for relief from Syria. Elisha’s last signs promise Joash victories over Syria.
chapters.13.lds: The older manual connects Elisha’s arrows with victories over Syria.
chapters.14.summary: Amaziah spares his enemies’ children. He wins in Edom but loses to Israel’s Joash. Jeroboam later restores Israel’s border.
chapters.14.meaning: Amaziah follows the law by sparing the children. His pride after victory leads to another costly war.
chapters.15.meaning: Repeated plots bring new kings to Israel. Assyrian demands then place heavy costs on the people.
chapters.16.meaning: Ahaz seeks Assyria’s help and copies an altar from Damascus. His alliance changes both Judah’s finances and worship.
chapters.16.lds: How does Ahaz’s need for foreign help change temple worship?
chapters.17.summary: Hoshea seeks Egypt’s help against Assyria. Assyria captures Samaria and removes its people. New settlers bring their own gods.
chapters.17.meaning: The book explains Israel’s fall through broken commitments to God. It then describes the mixed worship of new settlers.
chapters.18.meaning: Assyria attacks Judah and demands payment. Its spokesman tries to break the people’s trust in Hezekiah.
chapters.19.meaning: Hezekiah brings the threat to God. Isaiah promises relief, and Jerusalem survives the attack.
chapters.20.meaning: Hezekiah recovers and receives visitors from Babylon. Showing them his treasures leads to Isaiah’s warning.
chapters.21.meaning: Manasseh restores worship that Hezekiah removed. Unlike Chronicles, Kings gives no account of his repentance.
chapters.23.meaning: Josiah removes worship objects and renews Passover. His reforms do not prevent Judah’s later fall.
chapters.24.meaning: Babylon removes the king, workers, soldiers, and many families. The city loses people as well as treasures.
chapters.25.lds: What changes when Jehoiachin receives kindness at the end of the book?
people.mesha.meaning: Mesha sacrifices his son during the siege. The chapter then reports great wrath without naming whose wrath it is.
people.mesha-son.meaning: He is expected to follow Mesha as king. His father sacrifices him during the siege.
people.oil-sons.meaning: They bring empty jars while their mother pours oil. The sale pays the debt threatening their freedom.
people.shunammite-husband.meaning: He helps provide Elisha a room. His son later falls ill while visiting the harvest workers.
people.shunammite-son.role: Child whom Elisha brings back to life
people.shunammite-son.meaning: He dies after becoming ill in the fields. His mother seeks Elisha, who brings him back to life.
people.gehazi.meaning: Gehazi secretly accepts gifts Elisha refused. He later tells the king about the Shunammite’s child.
people.naaman.meaning: A captive girl and his servants guide him toward healing. He later asks for soil from Israel.
people.naaman-wife.meaning: Her servant girl tells her that a prophet in Samaria can help Naaman.
people.samaria-women.meaning: Their desperate agreement shows how deeply the siege harms families. One woman brings the complaint to the king.
people.four-men.meaning: They find the empty Syrian camp and eat. Then they decide the city must hear the good news.
people.samaria-officer.meaning: He doubts Elisha’s promise of food. He sees the relief but dies in the crowd at the gate.
people.jehonadab.meaning: Jehonadab joins Jehu’s chariot and accompanies him to Samaria.
people.jehosheba.meaning: Jehosheba hides Joash and his nurse from Athaliah. Chronicles also names her as Jehoiada’s wife.
people.jehozabad.meaning: Jehozabad joins the plot that kills Joash of Judah.
people.zibiah.meaning: The opening of Joash’s reign names Zibiah as his mother and Beersheba as her hometown.
people.jonah.meaning: Jonah’s message promises the restoration of Israel’s border. This notice comes during Jeroboam’s reign.
people.shalmaneser.meaning: Shalmaneser attacks Hoshea and lays siege to Samaria.
people.rabsaris.meaning: Rabsaris is one of the Assyrian officers sent against Jerusalem. The title does not give a personal name.
people.jedidah.meaning: Jedidah is Josiah’s mother. The chapter names her father and hometown.
people.hamutal.meaning: Hamutal is the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah. Her father Jeremiah comes from Libnah.
people.nehushta.meaning: Nehushta surrenders with Jehoiachin and goes into exile with the royal household.
people.zephaniah-priest.meaning: Babylon captures Zephaniah after Jerusalem falls. He is executed with other leaders at Riblah.
people.jaazaniah.meaning: Jaazaniah meets Gedaliah with the other army captains after Jerusalem’s fall.
people.elijah.meaning: Elijah leaves his cloak for Elisha. His earlier warnings also shape the fall of Ahab’s family.
people.elisha.meaning: Elisha helps families, heals Naaman, and confronts rulers. His work reaches both ordinary households and royal courts.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: Jehu destroys Ahab’s royal family and Baal’s temple. He keeps worshiping the golden calves.
people.jezebel.meaning: Jezebel confronts Jehu from a window. Her death fulfills Elijah’s earlier warning about her.
people.bethel-old-prophet.meaning: He lies to the visiting prophet and later mourns him. Josiah leaves their shared burial place undisturbed.
people.david.meaning: Kings measures later rulers against David’s faithfulness. God’s promise to his family also explains Judah’s continued rule.
people.tirhakah.meaning: News of Tirhakah’s approach reaches the Assyrian king during the threat to Jerusalem.
people.necho.role: Egyptian king who intervenes in Judah
people.zedekiah.meaning: Zedekiah rebels against Babylon and flees Jerusalem. Babylon captures him, kills his sons, and blinds him.
places.edom.summary: Amaziah defeats Edom before challenging Israel’s king.
places.gilead.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. Syria and Assyria take land in this region.
places.jericho.summary: Elisha visits Jericho and makes its bad water safe.
places.jerusalem.summary: Judah’s kings rule from Jerusalem. Babylon later destroys its walls, houses, and temple.
places.jordan.summary: Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan. Naaman later washes in it, and a lost axe head is recovered nearby.
